session_evaluation: The session's SHA-256 of the expected list (number, file, start, end, expected) equals the page's, so the screen built the windows the session expected and the rule graded against the right answers. 109 of the 112 windows holding an id were answered with it (97.3%), none of the 50 windows without one raised a false alarm. The three misses are among the four slices pass 9 missed under every setting (L-160).

first_attempt.reason: wave 1 call 1: rate_limited; wave 1 call 2: rate_limited
first_attempt.note: only 2 calls were in flight, so this was not the two-at-a-time limit. It came 56 minutes after pass 9 sent about 3.5 million characters in twelve minutes, and had cleared by 12:58 UTC the next day. What triggers it and how long it lasts are not measured.

limit_of_the_result: the screen is a rule that cannot miss for this question (every id contains DEC). A question no keyword can screen for gets no saving from this design.

rescored_2026-11-16.finding: All three misses were the rule's, not the model's. The check's pattern DEC-\d{3} has no boundary, so it matched the first seven characters of a longer token: DEC-100 inside DEC-1000 (M07.md, v2-parallel8/R6.md) and DEC-012 inside DEC-0123 (M13.md). In M07 the first true three-digit id is DEC-012, which is what the model answered; in the other two windows there is none, and the model said so.
rescored_2026-11-16.effect: exactly these three of the 162 windows change their expected answer; under the corrected rule the stored answers score 110 of 110 ids and 162 of 162 windows
rescored_2026-11-16.tier: derived: the same stored answers re-graded by the session against a corrected rule, not a new run and not graded by the page
